thread:
aj: heads up — noticed several GPU node pools are sitting at 0% GPU utilization overnight but cluster-autoscaler isn't removing the nodes. our bill spiked last midnight.

infra-bot: cluster-autoscaler[pid=2145] WARN: node "gpu-np-eu-3" unneeded but has non-evictable pods (pdb/nvidia-driver-lock, daemonset/nvidia-ds).

maria: can you paste the CA helm values and args? also which CA image/version?

aj: helm values excerpt:
```
controller:
  extraArgs:
    --expander=most-pods
    --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
    --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
    --balance-similar-node-groups=true
    --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true
    --max-empty-bulk-delete=5
```
CA image: k8s.gcr.io/cluster-autoscaler:v1.25.0
k8s cluster: 1.25.x

kevin: two quick notes: (1) most-pods tends to distribute pods across groups which is bad for single-gpu-per-node shapes, it leads to fragmentation; least-waste or priority can pack better. (2) PDBs will block eviction, CA respects them. check for any PDB that selects those driver or monitoring pods.

jun: we recently added a PDB for the driver installer to stop mass restarts during upgrades. looks like pdb/nvidia-driver-lock is the culprit per infra-bot. Also we use mixed spot/ondemand nodegroups which complicates CA behavior when spot instances are reclaimed.

maria: options to fix quickly:
- remove or relax the driver PDB selector so driver pods become evictable
- switch expander to least-waste for GPU nodegroups to encourage packing
- increase --scale-down-unneeded-time to 20m to tolerate short bursts
- lower --scale-down-utilization-threshold to 0.4 for GPU pools
- set --max-node-provision-time=10m so CA gives up faster on stuck provisioning attempts
- consider setting --max-empty-bulk-delete=1 for GPU pools to avoid accidental large deletions on preemptions

aj: i like that list. regarding mixed spot/ondemand: when spot preempts a few nodes CA spins up replacements often in different AZs/groups leading to cross-group imbalance. suggestions?

kevin: create separate nodegroups by purchase option and zone. label them and use the priority expander to prefer ondemand when spot availability is low. also set --balance-similar-node-groups=false for canary to reduce cross-group moves while we test.

jun: also think about a tiny per-zone buffer: min size 1 for GPU groups so we avoid slow cold starts for jobs that need GPUs urgently. cost vs latency tradeoff.

aj: immediate actionables I'm going to run tonight on eng-infra-canary:
- remove pdb/nvidia-driver-lock or change its selector to exclude the driver-installer pod
- switch expander to least-waste in canary
- set --scale-down-unneeded-time=20m and --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.4 for the gpu nodegroups
- add --max-node-provision-time=10m and lower --max-empty-bulk-delete to 1 for GPU nodegroups

maria: when you flip expander, monitor per-node-group cost and pod packing metrics. least-waste can increase cost if it prefers larger instance types that reduce waste but cost more per GPU-hour. keep an eye on the cost dashboard and tokenized-per-second metrics.

aj: i'll roll changes at 03:00 UTC to the canary and post back after 45 minutes. tagging oncall in case we need a rollback. :rotating_light:

sre-rotation: noted — we'll watch alerts and rollback if scale-down spikes or pod failures increase.

infra-bot: deploy job started for chart=cluster-autoscaler canary@eng-infra-canary by aj at 1763893456

aj: update 30m in: canary switched to least-waste and pdb relaxed. so far nodes are consolidating and two eu GPU nodes scaled down. cost preview shows small dip but still monitoring for spot churn. will report final after 2h.
